question: What is the first step in project planning?
incorrect_answers: Create a project schedule
Identify project stakeholders
Develop a project budget
reasoning: Defining the project scope is the first step in project planning because it sets the boundaries and deliverables of the project. It ensures that all stakeholders have a clear understanding of what the project will achieve and what is out of scope.

question: As an Agile Project Manager, what will you recommend to the executive team when there is confusion about product scope and the definition of done?
correct_answer: Encourage a self-organizing team to form, including the people who created the requirements and outcomes in the first place.
incorrect_answers: Select a person from each part of the organization to assist, to ensure diversity.
Have the functional manager select their friends or favorite team members.
Hire external consultants to run the project and create the product.
reasoning: Agile encourages self-organizing teams composed of the people who created the requirements and had the desired outcome in the first place. This gives a higher level of ownership and product expertise that often cannot be bought.

question: You are running an Agile project and meet with the team for the next sprint planning meeting. What will you do next?
correct_answer: The product owner shares the updated backlog, and the team discusses it to ensure a shared understanding.
incorrect_answers: Negotiate the scope and costs of the project with the project sponsor.
Walk through three questions with the team—what did I do yesterday? What will I do today? Is anything blocking me?
The dev team demonstrates the working feature to the product owner, who marks it as complete.
reasoning: The product owner should share the updated backlog items and ensure the entire team has a good understanding of how to move forward.

question: You are a project manager working on an Agile project and want your team to maximize the value they bring to the customer. What can you eliminate in order to maximize project value?
incorrect_answers: Daily stand-ups
Sprint reviews
Testing
reasoning: In addition to eliminating the introduction of unnecessary features, value can be maximized by eliminating partially done work, delays, extra processes and features, task switching, waiting, moving information or a deliverable, defects or rework, and handoffs.

question: You are working on a project and the team has recently moved to an Agile way of work. One of the team members is confused about Scrum and what typically happens after the sprint review. What will you tell them happens next?
correct_answer: Hold a sprint retrospective with the team
incorrect_answers: Perform product backlog refinement with the product owner
Perform story card elaboration with the three amigos (Business, Development, Testing)
Hold a Daily Scrum
reasoning: A sprint retrospective is held with the whole team after a sprint review but before the sprint planning meeting. It is used to gather lessons learned, look for opportunities for improvement, and ensure everyone has a voice for feedback and implementing improvements before the next sprint.

question: You are working in an Agile team and preparing the Agile team charter. You work with the Agile team to ensure the team charter answers these four questions: Why are we doing this project? Who benefits and how?
correct_answer: What does 'done' mean for the project? How are we going to work together?
incorrect_answers: When will the project end? What do we do with the product?
How much risk is on the project? What is the project scope?
How many defects are allowed in the product? How many testers are there?
reasoning: An Agile team charter typically covers why we are doing the project, who benefits and how, what 'done' looks like, and how we are going to work together.

question: You are working with a new Agile project manager and explain that Agile favors value-based measurements instead of predictive measurements on a project. What is an example of value-based measurements?
correct_answer: Feature burndown chart (features delivered) and customer satisfaction
incorrect_answers: Earned value management and the schedule performance index
Variance Analysis and the Estimate to Complete
Variance at Completion and the cost performance index
reasoning: Agile works with value delivered as its primary measurement. All the other options are predictive measurements from a traditional project management methodology.

question: Agile Unified Process (AUP) is an auxiliary Agile method that focuses on performing more iterative cycles across seven key disciplines and incorporating the associated feedback before formal delivery. Which is NOT one of the seven key disciplines within a release?
incorrect_answers: Discipline of the high level model
Discipline in testing
Discipline in configuration management
reasoning: Agile focuses on transparency to ensure the customer needs are met, not in specifically managing customer expectations.

question: You are leading a coaching session with your project team on the additional Agile and Lean frameworks that have contributed to the Agile way of work. What frameworks will you share with the team?
correct_answer: Scaled Agile Framework, Large Scale Scrum
incorrect_answers: Project Management Plan, Project Charter
Working Group Meetings, Project Post Mortems
Flow Charting, Affinity Diagrams
reasoning: Agile and lean frameworks include Scaled Agile Framework, Large Scale Scrum, Scrum of Scrums, Dynamic Systems Development Method, along with the more common Kanban, eXtreme Programming, and Scrum.

question: Crystal is an Agile framework focusing on individuals and their interactions, as opposed to processes and tools. It is not a set process but a guideline for team collaboration and communication. Which of the following is NOT one of its core beliefs?
incorrect_answers: Technologies change techniques
Cultures change norms
Distances change communication
reasoning: Crystal Clear describes the three core beliefs as technologies changing techniques, cultures changing norms, and distances changing communication. These beliefs support key Agile practices like stand-ups, collaborative user story creation, retrospectives, and the whole-team approach.

question: You are working on a project in the role of Scrum Master and have set a meeting with the team and the product owner to refine the product backlog. What should the team do in this meeting?
correct_answer: Estimate and refine the work items
incorrect_answers: Prioritize the work items
Add features to the project backlog
Identify fixes
reasoning: The product owner adjusts the priority of product backlog items, while the team is responsible for estimating and refining work items. Each time the team refines their estimates, they add a higher level of detail.

question: You are working with a team who would like to become Agile. The functional manager asks you what the difference between Kanban and Scrum is. What will you tell them?
correct_answer: Kanban teams employ a pull system.
incorrect_answers: Kanban teams plan their work in sprints or iterations.
There are no WIP limits in Kanban.
Kanban teams work on a project as a whole.
reasoning: The main difference between Scrum and Kanban is that Kanban teams employ a pull system. This means when an item of work is completed, it triggers someone to 'pull' the next item in the queue onto the board to work on. Kanban teams work off a Kanban board that displays each task and have a limit to how much work in progress (WIP) can be in place.

question: You are working on a new project with an Agile product development team, who have self-formed and chosen a Scrum Master called Jeremy. Jeremy immediately sets a meeting with the team to explain and flesh out their Team Charter. What has made Jeremy a good choice for Scrum Master?
correct_answer: He shows servant leadership and engages the team in decision-making.
incorrect_answers: He likes to work within set processes.
He has been with the company for more than five years.
He sticks to the plan and does not change.
reasoning: Jeremy shows the traits of servant leadership by engaging the team in team decisions, starting with the Team Charter and ground rules so everyone knows where they stand. By communicating the reasons for his decisions, he is a suitable Scrum Master and is less focused on command and control.

question: You are managing a project as an Agile project manager, and a business representative for the product you are delivering asks you how many defects were found in the latest round of testing. You don’t know the answer. What should you do?
correct_answer: Take him into the team area, where the 'information radiator' with project information is displayed.
incorrect_answers: Guess the number then change the subject.
Tell the business partner you will send an e-mail to him with the information.
Ask the business partner to call the Scrum Master to get a correct answer.
reasoning: A core component of Agile is Visual Management and transparency. Part of this are the various parts of the project information radiator (often physical, but can be tech-driven). This includes things such as team velocity, Kanban board, product backlog, burndown chart, latest test results and issues, and results of retrospectives.

question: You are working in a company that is moving from a Waterfall methodology to Agile. You mention to the business unit manager that the team will be better prepared to respond to change and meet the customer needs. Why is this?
correct_answer: The Agile team works directly with a business owner or representative to constantly prioritize delivered value.
incorrect_answers: The Agile team delivers the product all in one go.
The Agile team is for developers only, so development will improve.
The business partners review statuses and ask for recommendations.
reasoning: Working with business partners or someone who represents the customer almost daily is a key part of Agile. The team hears what the business would like the results to be, and meeting face-to-face is better than reading requirements, documents, emails, or even a conference call.

question: For Agile life-cycles, two kinds of planning occur: release planning and iteration planning. In release planning, business representatives establish and prioritize the user stories for the release in collaboration with the team, refining larger user stories into a collection of smaller stories. What is the INCORRECT description below regarding iteration planning and backlog preparation?
correct_answer: The project coach encourages the team to work alone, so no one bothers them.
incorrect_answers: The backlog is the ordered list of all the work, presented in 'story' form, for a team.
The facilitator encourages the team to work in triads of a developer, tester, and product owner/business analyst.
The triad discuss, write, and then place enough stories into an iteration, ensuring enough features for a first release.
reasoning: Answers A, C, and D are correct in describing backlog preparation for iteration planning. The incorrect statement is B because Agile encourages collaboration and teamwork, not isolation.
